leaving-germany-exit-tax.old: **Which shares.** Shares within § 17(1) sentence 1 EStG. § 17(1) sentence 3 defines them: shares (Aktien), GmbH shares, profit participation rights (Genussscheine) and similar participations, rights to acquire such shares, and shares in a company that opted to be taxed as a corporation under § 1a KStG. Shares in a cooperative also count (§ 17(7) EStG). § 6(1) AStG applies subject to the rules of the Income Tax Act, the Corporation Tax Act and the Reorganisation Tax Act, so shares held as business assets need a separate check (see "When to refuse or refer").
leaving-germany-exit-tax.new:
**Which shares.** Shares within § 17(1) sentence 1 EStG. § 17(1) sentence 3 defines them: shares (Aktien), GmbH shares, profit participation rights (Genussscheine) and similar participations, rights to acquire such shares, and shares in a company that opted to be taxed as a corporation under § 1a KStG. Shares in a cooperative also count (§ 17(7) EStG). § 6(1) AStG applies subject to the rules of the Income Tax Act, the Corporation Tax Act and the Reorganisation Tax Act, so shares held as business assets need a separate check (see "When to refuse or refer").

**Recent free acquisition: combined-source interpretation.** Read § 6(1) AStG's reference to § 17(1) sentence 1 EStG together with § 17(1) sentence 4, which expressly applies sentence 1 to the following predecessor case. If the relevant share was acquired free of charge within the five years before the deemed disposal, a holder who did not personally meet the 1% test must still be tested where the predecessor, or an earlier predecessor in a chain of free transfers, met that participation test within the relevant five-year period under sentence 1. Record the acquisition and each relevant transfer date, direct/indirect holdings and the predecessor's qualifying holding dates. A recent gift or inheritance of a 0.5% share therefore does not fail solely because the current holder never reached 1%, if the qualifying predecessor test is met. This is a separate shareholding rule from the residence-period aggregation in § 6(2) AStG; all other person, trigger and tax-chain conditions still apply.

de-trade-tax.new:
**6. Apportion between municipalities (Zerlegung).** If the business had permanent establishments in more than one municipality during the period, or one establishment spans two, or it moved, the tax office splits the base amount ([§ 28(1) GewStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/gewstg/__28.html)). The key uses the qualifying statutory wages of each establishment under § 31, then rounds them down to full EUR 1,000 ([§ 29 GewStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/gewstg/__29.html)). Where the business is not run by a legal person, EUR 25,000 a year in total is added as wages for the working owners ([§ 31(5) GewStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/gewstg/__31.html)). Wind, solar and storage businesses use installed capacity for nine tenths (§ 29(1) no. 2 and 3). Each municipality then applies its own multiplier to its share ([§ 4(1) GewStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/gewstg/__4.html)).

**Qualifying apportionment wages (§ 31(1)–(4) GewStG).** Start with employment remuneration under § 19(1) no. 1 EStG, excluding amounts exempt from income tax under other legislation. Include overtime and Sunday, public-holiday and night-work supplements regardless of their income-tax treatment. Exclude remuneration paid to people employed for vocational training and one-off remuneration calculated by profit. For each individual employee, exclude the remaining remuneration above EUR 50,000. Where the business is partly trade-tax exempt, exclude pay of employees who do not work exclusively or predominantly in the taxable business or part. Apply these employee rules before aggregating the establishment's qualifying wages and applying the § 29 rounding and apportionment key. The separate total EUR 25,000 working-owner amount under § 31(5) remains as stated above.

For a stipulated ordinary corporation with two establishments, one employee at A paid EUR 100,000 and one at B paid EUR 50,000, with no trainee pay, profit-based bonus or other adjustment, qualifying wages are EUR 50,000 at each establishment. A EUR 1,000 base amount therefore splits EUR 500 to each, before each municipality applies its own multiplier. The uncapped 2:1 salary ratio is not the statutory key.

de-einkommensteuer-freelancer.old: - § 7g needs the asset used in a domestic establishment (§ 7g(4)).
de-einkommensteuer-freelancer.new: - Under § 7g, the own-use alternative requires the qualifying business use in a domestic establishment; letting is a separate statutory alternative for the required period (§ 7g(1), (4), (6)). Apply the main method's other asset, profit, timing, use and reporting conditions to the actual arrangement; this does not establish eligibility for a particular foreign leasing arrangement.
de-einkommensteuer-freelancer.reason: DE-R14 align cross-border summary with exact existing main method

de-einkommensteuer-freelancer.old: if such income is not more than EUR 410 in total it is taken off again.
de-einkommensteuer-freelancer.new: the separate § 46(3) deduction covers eligible taxable non-wage income not assessed under § 32d(6), where that eligible income totals no more than EUR 410. Reduce the deduction by the part of the age-relief amount exceeding the wage-based component under § 24a sentence 5, using wages excluding § 19(2) pension remuneration, and by the § 13(3) amount (§ 46(3) sentence 2).
de-einkommensteuer-freelancer.reason: DE-R16 actual eligible-income exclusion and statutory reduction components
